required_tables.commit: Python regions and HIP API calls from pytorch_function_fit.py, run with '-e 200'.
required_tables.name: regions

validation_queries.description: Verify that 'train_one_epoch' ran once per epoch.
validation_queries.error_message: 'train_one_epoch' was not traced 200 times, one per epoch requested with '-e 200'.
validation_queries.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM regions WHERE name = 'train_one_epoch';

validation_queries.description: Verify kernel launches reached the HIP API.
validation_queries.error_message: Almost no hipLaunchKernel calls found; the training loop should launch kernels on the device.
validation_queries.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM regions WHERE name = 'hipLaunchKernel';

validation_queries.description: Verify the batch uploads reached the HIP API.
validation_queries.error_message: Almost no hipMemcpyWithStream calls found; each step copies its inputs and targets to the device.
validation_queries.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM regions WHERE name = 'hipMemcpyWithStream';

validation_queries.description: Check for any NULL values in the 'name' column of regions.
validation_queries.error_message: NULL entries found in the name column of regions.
validation_queries.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM regions WHERE name IS NULL;

required_tables.commit: GPU kernels dispatched by the model. The counts below only establish that each part of the model reached the device, deliberately not how much of it ran: how many kernels a training step issues depends on the epoch count, the batch size and whatever torch does internally, so a real run clears these by orders of magnitude. Matching is by substring because the torch kernel names are mangled C++ templates whose exact spelling changes between releases.
required_tables.name: kernels

validation_queries.description: Verify kernels were dispatched to the GPU at all.
validation_queries.error_message: Almost no kernel dispatches found; the model did not run on the device.

validation_queries.description: Verify the dispatches are not all one kernel: a GEMM, an activation and the optimizer update are distinct.
validation_queries.error_message: Fewer than 3 distinct kernel names found; the trace is missing part of the training step.

validation_queries.description: Verify the nn.Linear layers reached rocBLAS. Tensile names every generated GEMM 'Cijk_<layout>_<tile>_...'.
validation_queries.error_message: Almost no rocBLAS GEMM kernels found; the nn.Linear layers did not reach rocBLAS.
validation_queries.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM kernels WHERE name LIKE 'Cijk%';

validation_queries.description: Verify the activations ran on the device: the nn.Tanh layers are elementwise kernels.
validation_queries.error_message: Almost no tanh kernels found; the nn.Tanh activations did not run on the device.
validation_queries.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM kernels WHERE name LIKE '%tanh%';

validation_queries.description: Verify the batch uploads happened. Torch stages small host-to-device transfers through a ROCclr blit kernel rather than an async copy, so the input and target batch of every step land here instead of in memory_copies.
validation_queries.error_message: Almost no copy-buffer kernels found; the input and target batches were not uploaded to the device.
validation_queries.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM kernels WHERE name LIKE '%copyBuffer%';

validation_queries.description: Check for kernels with no active time.
validation_queries.error_message: Kernels with no active execution times found.
validation_queries.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM kernels WHERE (end - start) = 0;

validation_queries.description: Check for null kernel names in the summary.
validation_queries.error_message: Found kernels with null names in top_kernels.
validation_queries.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM top_kernels WHERE name IS NULL;

validation_queries.description: Check that the summary is not empty.

required_tables.commit: Only a couple of transfers reach the memory copy domain, and they come from moving the model to the device rather than from the training loop. The per-step batch uploads are staged through a blit kernel instead, and are checked in the kernels table above.
required_tables.name: memory_copies

validation_queries.description: Verify at least one real host-to-device copy was recorded.
validation_queries.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM memory_copies WHERE name = 'MEMORY_COPY_HOST_TO_DEVICE';
